attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'as far as I can tell' hedge on 'inevitable' and the firm 'yet to disappear' part. Treating it as an observation fits the checkable part.

contract.note: Only the firm part is scored: hallucinations had not disappeared by mid-2024. The hedged inevitability opinion is left out. The 2024 window up to the post date is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Independent Stanford RegLab/HAI study, May 2024. Legal AI tools marketed as hallucination-free still hallucinated on 17% to 34%+ of queries.
News report dated July 2024: OpenAI's SearchGPT demo gave wrong festival dates, days before the post.

reviews.rationale: Two items from inside the period show leading LLM products still hallucinating, including products that claimed to avoid it: an independent study and a news report. Nothing in the packet suggests hallucinations had been eliminated by mid-2024. The inevitability opinion is hedged and not scored.

attribution.note: A bullet point Marcus wrote and endorsed as one of his reasons.

semantics.note: He states it in the present tense, as a fact. The proposition matches it, and 'generative AI' follows from the surrounding text.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure. The plain reading, that meaningful capability gains across frontier releases had stalled, is the ordinary meaning of 'plateau'. Using the latest quarter before the post is a reasonable choice. The result depends on that reading, but it is not stretched.

evidence.note: Independent LMSYS arena, June 2024. GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 scored notably higher than GPT-4 Turbo and Gemini 1.5 Pro. It measures user preference and is mainly vision, but the votes fall inside the period.
Independent preprint, June 2024: a clear performance gap favouring the newer models on Olympiad-level problems. It also says overall performance is still unsatisfactory.
Anthropic's own internal coding evaluation: 64% vs 38%. This is a company disclosure, so it only corroborates the independent items.

reviews.rationale: Independent comparisons from April to June 2024 show meaningful capability gains in GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet over their predecessors on the same evaluations. A company disclosure corroborates this. Continued shortcomings do not amount to a plateau in capability, so on the plain reading the claim is contradicted for that period.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Strong intuition' together with 'simply never going to' expresses high confidence, so it counts as a firm forecast. The 'at least not in the general form' scope is kept.

contract.note: 'Never' has no deadline, so the claim can only be contradicted early, by broad evidence of near-zero error rates. 'Reliably' has no stated threshold; the contract's reading is reasonable and its ambiguity flags are noted.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own statement, Sept 2025, that hallucinations persist in its models. This is a company disclosure and cannot confirm 'never'.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No dated event in the packet meets the early-contradiction rule (near-zero hallucination across broad tasks), and no finite date can confirm 'never'. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle it.

contract.note: 'Killer app' has no stated threshold. The plain reading, compelling value plus substantial sustained demand, is ordinary. Letting a professional application qualify is a choice the contract flags. The result depends on that threshold.

evidence.note: Independent survey, March–April 2024: infrequent ChatGPT use. Low use across the population does not show that no compelling application existed.
Microsoft's own report on Copilot subscribers and customer benefits for the quarter ending March 2024. It is a company disclosure from before the target period.

reviews.rationale: The packet has nothing that establishes, inside April–June 2024, either an application with sustained demand and compelling value or broad evidence that none existed. The survey data is mixed, and the coding-assistant figures come from Microsoft and an earlier period. Neither settles the claim.
